name.description: The name of the action is the key by which it is accessed.

typeName.description:
The type against which the action should be dispatched. If not specified, this is the same as the source type of
the parent view.

actionName.description: Name of the target C3 action

args.description:
The specification for how to build the arguments to the action. Each entry in the map corresponds to a single
parameter of the action method and its value is the specification of the value as an object hierarchy. All required
parameters must have a specification here so that the action can be dispatched.

If a value, at top level or within an object value, is a string, that string is the view field name from which the
actual value is taken. If a literal string is desired, it must be quoted twice.

```json
{
  "name": "force-commit",
  "action": "commit",
  "args": {
    "this": "this",
    "spec": {
      "comment": "'force-commit from UI'",
      "force": true
    }
  }
}
```

In the example above, the "this" parameter refers to the instance of the Obj managed by the model on which the
action is invoked. Expressions rooted with "this" always refer to the model object (never the #argsView).

The "spec" parameter is an object of which fields are specified:
 - `comment` has a string literal, which must be double-quoted to avoid being interpreted as a view field name
 - `force` has a boolean literal (all non-string values are assumed to be literals)

Note that field values normally refer to the view on which the action is invoked, but if a custom view is used to
prompt for the values, field names refer to #argsView.

sourceType.description: The type for the {@link UiView} which this UiViewAction is part of.

title:
A "view action" is the declaration of a button/menu item action available to the user of a UI hosted on the view.
It defines now arguments are assembled from the model instance on which the action is invoked to build a call to the
associated method.

@see UiView
name: UiViewAction
